subject: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options — Acme Payments PII handling
messages:
From: Aisha Thompson <aisha.thompson@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Encryption and KMS questions from today's call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier — good overview. We're trying to complete a security checklist for PII flows and had a few follow-ups specifically on encryption and key management:

- In-transit: are you terminating TLS at your edge? Do you support TLS 1.3 only?
- At-rest: what algorithms/keys are used for data at rest (customer data + logs)?
- Customer-managed keys: can we bring our own keys (BYOK)? Do you support HSM-backed keys?
- Key rotation / lifecycle: what's the rotation cadence and can we trigger rotations?
- Audit/logging: are key usage events logged and available to customers?
- Data residency: if we use Dedicated or Private deployment, can keys and encrypted blobs be kept in our VPC/region?

We're collecting answers to decide whether to include Redwood in our vendor shortlist. If you can send a short recap and any diagrams/policy docs, that would be great.

Thanks —
Aisha Thompson
Security Lead, Acme Payments
aisha.thompson@acmepayments.com

Attachment: security-checklist.xlsx (referenced in call)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Thompson <aisha.thompson@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption and KMS questions from today's call

Hi Aisha —

Great talking earlier. Below is a concise recap addressing your list; happy to expand in a technical deep-dive. I've looped in Marcus (Solutions Eng) and Priya (Product Security) for any implementation specifics and to join the follow-up.

Recap / Answers (summary):

- In-transit: We use TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 enabled by default at our public edge. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers can terminate TLS in their VPC if they prefer.

- At-rest: All customer payloads are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Token caches and KV stores are encrypted with keys managed by the deployment's KMS integration (see below).

- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): Supported. We integrate with AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault for BYOK workflows. For Dedicated and Private deployments, we support HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM, Cloud KMS HSM tiers) and can surface CMK usage to customer audit logs.

- HSM support: Yes — HSM-backed keys are supported where the cloud provider offers them. For air-gapped/private on-prem installs, we can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) during onboarding.

- Key rotation / lifecycle: Rotation can be automated via customer KMS policies. Customers may also trigger rotations manually; Redwood performs re-encryption of short-term caches without downtime where possible. We recommend rotation cadence aligned to your internal policy (e.g., 90 days).

- Audit / Logging: Key usage events (encrypt/decrypt/sign) are recorded in Redwood audit logs with timestamps, requester identity, and request context. For Hosted customers, logs are viewable in the Console and exportable via our logging API. For Dedicated/Private, logs can be shipped to your SIEM or kept in your VPC.

- Data residency: For Dedicated and Private deployments, data (and KMS integrations) can be pinned to your region/VPC. Hosted workloads by default are processed in the region you select; if strict residency is required we recommend Dedicated or Private.

Attached: redwood-kms-arch.png (high-level KMS integration diagram), redwood-soc2-evidence-summary.pdf (SOC 2 summary + controls relevant to encryption).

Next steps we propose:
1) Schedule a 60-min security deep-dive with our product security and solutions team (Marcus + Priya).
2) Share any vendor security questionnaire (we'll pre-fill and return within 3 business days).
3) If you want a proof-of-concept, we can stand up a Dedicated eval with BYOK for a short-term test.

Please let us know preferred times for the deep-dive.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the deep-dive: 

- BYOK lifecycle: if we revoke a key on our KMS, will Redwood immediately lose access to historical artifacts encrypted with that key? How do you manage long-term archives?
- HSM verification: do you provide an attestation/certificate that keys are HSM-protected (e.g., CloudHSM attestation) for Dedicated deployments?
- Logs: can we get a signed/exportable audit trail for key usage for the past 12 months?
- Private deployment: for our compliance team, is it possible to keep both keys and encrypted blob storage entirely within our VPC (no egress to Redwood-managed storage)?

Also attaching our abbreviated security questionnaire and a short timeline for procurement. If you can answer these points in the deep-dive, that should cover most of our open items.

Regards,
Aisha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption and KMS questions from today's call

Hi Aisha —

Great questions. Short answers here and we'll cover the details in the deep-dive.

- Revocation & historical artifacts: If you revoke a CMK in your KMS, access to newly requested decrypt operations will fail. For historical artifacts, we recommend one of two approaches: (1) Maintain a key retention policy in your KMS for archived objects (best for long-term auditability), or (2) use a key-rotation-with-wrapping strategy where a root CMK wraps data keys; you can rotate wrapped keys while preserving ability to decrypt if wrapped keys are retained. We'll walk through trade-offs during the deep-dive and can provide a migration plan for archived data.

- HSM attestation: For cloud HSM services (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, GCP HSM), we can surface provider attestation metadata. For Dedicated deployments we can include HSM attestation artifacts as part of the onboarding package — Priya will coordinate the exact evidence.

- Signed/exportable audit trail: Yes — for Dedicated/Private customers we can export key usage logs (with signatures) to your SIEM or to a storage location you control for the retention window you need. Hosted customers have an API to pull audit logs and we can discuss signed exports if required.

- Private deployment full isolation: Yes — Private/on-prem installs can keep both key material and encrypted blob storage entirely within your environment. Redwood's control plane can be configured to avoid holding any plaintext or key material. We'll share an architecture diagram specific to that setup in the deep-dive.

Action items / next steps:
- Marcus: can you propose 2x 60-min slots next week for the technical deep-dive (include a calendar invite with conference bridge + placeholder dial-in)?
- Priya: please prepare HSM attestation examples and the list of audit exports we can provide.
- Aisha: please send any additional questions from your procurement timeline so we can align.

I'll also attach our standard BYOK onboarding checklist and a short-runbook for Dedicated evals in the deep-dive doc.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Best,
